fields.Front: Why is Node.js described as non-blocking / asynchronous I/O?
fields.Back: Node uses a single-threaded event loop plus libuv's thread pool: I/O operations (file, network, DB) are dispatched and their callbacks run later when complete, so the main thread never blocks waiting on them.

fields.Front: What is the Node.js event loop?
fields.Back: A loop that continuously checks for and executes queued callbacks (timers, I/O completions, immediates) in phases, letting a single JS thread handle many concurrent operations without blocking.

fields.Front: What's the key difference between CommonJS require() and ES Modules import in Node.js?
fields.Back: require() loads modules synchronously and resolves at call time (can be conditional/dynamic); ESM import is statically analyzed at parse time and needs "type": "module" or a .mjs extension to use natively.

fields.Front: How do you code a minimal Express server with a GET route?
fields.Back:
const express = require('express');
const app = express();

app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
  res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok' });
});

app.listen(3000);
A function with the signature (req, res, next) that runs during the request/response cycle — it can inspect or modify req/res, end the cycle, or call next() to pass control to the next middleware.

In an Express route handler, what do req.params, req.query, and req.body each represent?
fields.Back: req.params: named URL path segments (e.g. /users/:id); req.query: the URL's query string key/values; req.body: the parsed request payload (needs a body-parsing middleware like express.json()).

fields.Front: How do you code an Express route that reads a route param and a query param?
fields.Back:
app.get('/users/:id', (req, res) => {
  const { id } = req.params;
  const { active } = req.query;
  res.json({ id, active });
});

fields.Front: What is a Node.js stream, and why use one for large files instead of reading the whole file into memory?
fields.Back: A stream processes data in chunks over time (Readable, Writable, Duplex, Transform); it keeps memory usage low and lets processing start before the whole source has been read, unlike fs.readFile.

What does the package.json "dependencies" vs "devDependencies" distinction control?
fields.Back: dependencies are required at runtime in production; devDependencies are only needed for development, build, or test tooling and aren't installed with npm install --production.

fields.Front: What does package-lock.json guarantee that a version range in package.json (e.g. ^4.2.0) doesn't?
fields.Back: It pins the exact resolved version (and full dependency tree) that was installed, so every install reproduces identical dependency versions across machines and CI.

fields.Front: What's the idiomatic way to load environment-specific config (like DB URLs or API keys) into a Node.js app?
fields.Back: Read from process.env, typically populated via a .env file loaded with a package like dotenv in development, and via real environment variables injected by the platform/CI in production — keeping secrets out of source control.

fields.Front: Why can a single slow synchronous CPU-bound function block an entire Node.js server, even though I/O is non-blocking?
fields.Back: Node runs JS on a single main thread; a long synchronous computation occupies that thread, so the event loop can't process other pending callbacks (other requests) until it finishes.

fields.Front: In a Discord bot doing CRUD against a SQL backend (Node.js), why use parameterized queries instead of string-concatenating user input into SQL?
fields.Back: Parameterized queries send user input separately from the SQL statement so the driver escapes it, preventing SQL injection from untrusted Discord command input.

fields.Front: For a BMO-style Node.js backend modernized into serverless AWS Lambda functions, why does minimizing an Express app's dependencies matter for cold starts?
fields.Back: Each Lambda cold start must load and initialize the Node.js runtime and all required modules before handling the first request, so fewer/lighter dependencies directly reduce cold-start latency.

fields.Text: The Node.js event loop processes phases in this order each tick: {{c1::timers}} → pending callbacks → idle/prepare → {{c2::poll}} (I/O) → {{c3::check}} (setImmediate) → close callbacks.
